trust_decision.summary: Whether a client TLS object will verify the peer's identity: the C layer configures hostname verification only when a server_hostname is passed, so a context with check_hostname=True plus no hostname verifies the chain but not the name; wrap_socket() refused this in Python, wrap_bio() did not.

landing_point.why: The summary names SSLContext.wrap_bio(); it sits next to wrap_socket(), whose _create already carries the check at Lib/ssl.py:1018-1019.

fix_sites.entry_point: new helper ssl._check_sslobject_params (Lib/ssl.py), shared by both constructors

ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio() -> SSLObject._create (Lib/ssl.py:470, Lib/ssl.py:813); also asyncio SSLProtocol via Lib/asyncio/sslproto.py:330 (loop.create_connection/start_tls/open_connection/StreamWriter.start_tls)
ssl.SSLContext.wrap_socket() -> SSLSocket._create (Lib/ssl.py:456, Lib/ssl.py:1006); refactor only, behaviour unchanged

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All source changes are in Lib/ssl.py (fix.diff:10052-10103). asyncio picks up the check through wrap_bio (Lib/asyncio/sslproto.py:330) with no asyncio source change; only asyncio docs/tests changed (fix.diff:9991-10018, fix.diff:10104-10155).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The C entry Modules/_ssl.c:4990 (_SSLContext._wrap_bio) is underscore-private, and the .context setter (Lib/ssl.py:829-831, Modules/_ssl.c:2360-2377) is documented for server-side SNI callbacks (Modules/_ssl.c:2338-2343), so a solver can argue either one is not a public client route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: check_hostname=False with no server_hostname must keep working, both for wrap_bio and for asyncio's ssl=True default context, which turns check_hostname off when no name is given. Server-side wrap_bio with no hostname must keep working too. If a fix rejects a missing hostname unconditionally, or puts the check in C for every client object, it breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: server_hostname='' with check_hostname=True (fails on the asyncio route, which turns '' into None at Lib/asyncio/sslproto.py:299-302; direct wrap_bio already failed in C at Modules/_ssl.c:839-845)

O7_producer.where: Hostname verification parameters are set by Modules/_ssl.c:825-888 only at construction time (Modules/_ssl.c:988-993); there is no serializer, schema or cache.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Swapping a check_hostname=True context onto an existing client SSLObject/SSLSocket created without a hostname; the setter calls SSL_set_SSL_CTX without configuring verification of the host, so check_hostname reports True but the name is never checked.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The setter is documented for server-side SNI callbacks (Modules/_ssl.c:2338-2343), and the advisory talks only about constructor parameters.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Python wrapper is in Lib/ssl.py:829-831 and Lib/ssl.py:1110-1113; the sink is in another language and file (Modules/_ssl.c)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Direct call to the C method _ssl._SSLContext._wrap_bio / _wrap_socket with check_hostname=True and server_hostname=None; the Python-level check is never reached.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The underscore marks it as a private API that only ssl.py calls.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Modules/_ssl.c, separate C extension from the Lib/ssl.py landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Setting ctx.check_hostname=True after wrap_bio/wrap_socket has already created the object with no hostname; the C code reads the flag only at construction.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Changing a context after it has been used is the caller's mistake and is not a constructor-parameter problem.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second asyncio TLS protocol (for example a legacy or proactor-specific one) that calls context._wrap_bio directly to set owner/session and skips SSLContext.wrap_bio.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: asyncio already reimplements the TLS state machine over memory BIOs; a maintainer chasing performance or owner semantics could plausibly bypass the public wrapper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SSLSocket._real_connect re-creates _sslobj from self.server_hostname; a planted connect-time path that accepts a per-connect hostname override could skip _check_sslobject_params.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Deferred-connect sockets already build the C object outside _create, so a maintainer could add a hostname override there.

O9_family: TLS certificate / hostname verification bypass (CWE-297, improper validation of certificate with host mismatch)

O10_build.toolchain: CPython ./configure && make with OpenSSL headers (the change itself is pure Python in Lib/ssl.py)
O10_build.project_tests: Lib/test/test_ssl.py (SSLObjectTests, SSLErrorTests, ContextTests), Lib/test/test_asyncio/test_sslproto.py; all in-memory BIO tests, no network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the wrap_socket check into SSLContext.wrap_bio() or SSLObject._create and stop, leaving the C _wrap_bio and the .context setter unguarded.

out_of_scope_notes: Six of the 13 listed fix commits (acb4dc12..8a8eb0b9) are release/backport bundles that touch many unrelated files and other gh-issues; the advisory's own source change is 1697ea38 and its backports (641390146a, 966bf426, f4e43ba5, 869069d5, 5867d4e4, bdebbf9b).

The comment at Lib/asyncio/base_events.py:1093-1095 documents server_hostname='' as a bypass of the hostname check, but the fix's asyncio test (fix.diff:10124-10143) shows it now raises when the user context has check_hostname=True.
